images.caption: Figure 2:Comparison of alignment paradigms.(a)Flow-GRPOrelies on trajectory-level policy gradients from terminal rewards. (b)Flow-OPDrequires a pretrained teacher for step-wise MSE supervision. (c)Self-OPD (Ours)turns local stochastic branches and a self-reference baseline into dense pull-push supervision, without requiring any teacher.

Figure 3:Self-OPD pipeline.Top:The student branches its prediction intoKKSDE paths (blue), generates images via ODE rollouts (purple), and scores them (r+,rref,r−r^{+},r^{\mathrm{ref}},r^{-}).Bottom-left:Rewards define a self-referenced advantageAkA_{k}that pulls toward high-reward velocitiesv+v_{+}and pushes away from low-reward velocitiesv−v_{-}.Bottom-right:A direction-aware coefficientdkd_{k}gates the push to prevent it from counteracting the pull, resulting in the multi-branch lossℒSelf-OPD\mathcal{L}_{\text{Self-OPD}}.

Figure 5:Qualitative comparison.Each method uses its mixed-reward model if available, or the prompt-specific reward model (e.g., OCR for text prompts). Self-OPD achieves superior performance in both accuracy and aesthetics.
Figure 8:Strict vs. continuous scoringon “a photo of a white handbag and a red giraffe”. (a) base; (b) Self-OPD.

Figure 9:Aesthetic quality on GenEval prompts.Each method uses its mixed-reward model if available, or its GenEval-trained model otherwise (Flow-GRPO, GRPO-Guard). Self-OPD satisfies the compositional requirements (counting, spatial relations, attributes) while generating images with higher aesthetic quality, consistent with its higher PickScore/HPSv2 in Tab.2.

Figure 10:Aesthetic quality on OCR prompts.Each method uses its mixed-reward model if available, or its OCR-trained model otherwise (Flow-GRPO, GRPO-Guard). Self-OPD renders the target text accurately while producing more visually appealing scenes with richer backgrounds and realistic details.
